mechanism_narrative: A low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) relative to its 10-year average compresses the discount rate for equity valuation, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of instances when FEDFUNDS is below 4.0% (10-year average) over a 5-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the federal funds rate above 5.0% per annum signals monetary tightening, increasing discount rates and reducing equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS exceeds 5.0% over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Joint increases in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) indicate a tightening monetary cycle with rising inflation, which reduces real equity valuations and causes negative S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises > 0.2pp and CPIAUCSL rises > 0.1pp in 3 months
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL rise as specified over a 5-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a monetary tightening cycle (defined by FEDFUNDS > 4.5% and CPIAUCSL > 2.5% annually), increased cost of capital and inflationary pressure reduce equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when the regime condition is met over a 5-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Strong GDP growth (GDPC1) relative to its 5-year average indicates robust economic activity, increasing corporate earnings and driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of instances when GDPC1 growth exceeds 3.0% annually over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in the unemployment rate below 4.5% per annum signals tight labor markets, increasing wage pressures and corporate profit margins, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE falls below 4.5% over a 4-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in industrial production (INDPRO) and housing starts (HOUST) indicate a weakening supply chain and reduced manufacturing activity, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days due to lower corporate output.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls > 0.5% and HOUST falls > 1.0% in 3 months
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when both INDPRO and HOUST decline as specified over a 5-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion (defined by high GDP growth and high housing starts), sustained corporate earnings growth drives positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days, but only when the economy is near full capacity.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of instances when the late-cycle expansion condition is met over a 3-year rolling window.
